Subject: Redwood benchmark & recommended models — Acme Health follow-up

Hi Sofia / Carlos,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the context on the patient triage use case and the SLAs you need for triage-summarization (p95 < 250ms for short summaries, and sustained throughput of ~300 TPS during working hours). Below is a quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate model fit on a small sample set.

Recap:
- Primary intent: auto-summarize clinician notes + surface structured triage flags.
- Quality bar: >= 92 F1 on entity extraction from your sample prompts (rough target).
- Latency/throughput: p95 <= 250ms for short responses, baseline throughput 300 TPS.
- Data constraints: PHI-sensitive; prefer Private deployment or Dedicated with customer keys.

Recommended models for initial eval: (we'll run benchmarks with your prompt set)
- rw-medium-1 (quantized) — good balance of quality/cost for extraction tasks.
- rw-large-1 (fp16) — higher accuracy; we expect ~5-8% higher F1 for complex prompts.
- open-bison-1 (fallback) — lower cost, good for non-sensitive background tasks.

What I'll share now:
- Benchmark pack: Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS and latency percentiles) for the recommended variants. Link below + attached PDF/CSV.
- Prompt set: please see attached acme_prompt_set_v1.zip (10 representative clinician notes and evaluation labels).
- Next steps: If you’re good, we'll run a 48-hour eval on Dedicated with your prompt set and send a detailed report (quality metrics + latency percentiles + configuration recommended).

Are you available for a 30-minute sync on Wed (6/30) to review the benchmark findings? If so, which time window works best PST?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Sofia — great questions. Short answers up front, details below.

Short answers:
- rw-large-1 (fp16) observed numbers (from Redwood-verified perf tests):
  - single-request p50/p95/p99: 28ms / 180ms / 420ms (short summaries, 128 tokens)
  - sustained 300 TPS (continuous batching + KV cache behavior): p50/p95/p99: 42ms / 220ms / 560ms
- 48-hour eval on Dedicated with VPC peering + customer-managed keys: yes, we can do that — we'll route through your VPC and use the provided KMS material.

Details and attachments: I've attached the Redwood-verified performance profiles (redwood-performance-profiles.csv) and a summary PDF (redwood-acme-benchmarks-20260628.pdf). The CSV includes per-model rows with: model_variant, hw_type, sequence_len, batch_policy, TPS_peak, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms. Example excerpt: 

"model_variant=rw-large-1, hw_type=A100-80GB, seq_len=128, policy=continuous-batching, tps_peak=340, p50_ms=42, p95_ms=220, p99_ms=560"

Notes on how we benchmark:
- We simulate your request mix using your prompt set (attached) and a 60/40 split of short/long responses.
- Continuous batching optimizes throughput while keeping latency SLOs; we include KV cache priming for multi-turn threads where applicable.
- For PHI workflows we recommend Dedicated with encryption-in-transit and your own customer keys. Private (on-prem/VPC) is also an option if your compliance team prefers an air-gapped solution.

Next steps I propose:
1) We confirm the expanded prompt set you'll share tonight.
2) We spin up a 48-hour Dedicated eval (RDW-ACME-EVAL) using rw-large-1 and rw-medium-1.
3) After the run we deliver a report with: quality metrics (precision/recall/F1), latency percentiles by seq_len bucket, and recommended config (batch size, cache TTL).

Scheduling: Wed 6/30 afternoon PST works — propose 2:30pm PST. If that’s OK I’ll send a calendar invite with the agenda.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Alex — adding a couple practical notes from the eval/quality side:  

- Prompt sets: The attached acme_prompt_set_v1.zip is a good start. For the eval run we recommend: 1) tagging prompts by type (summary vs extraction), 2) including 150-200 labeled examples for stable quality stats, and 3) adding a small set of adversarial examples we've seen break entity extraction (ambiguity in abbreviations, mixed punctuation).
- Quality regression: we'll baseline rw-medium-1 and rw-large-1. If we see a >3% drop in F1 from expected on the labeled set we'll flag it and run a quick ablation (prompt tweaks + model variant comparison). Those gates are automated in our eval harness.
- Config recommendation (initial): rw-large-1 (fp16) for the production-critical path with batching policy = continuous, target batch latency = 50ms. rw-medium-1 (quant) as warm fallback for cost control.

Sofia — we'll join the Wed call and walk through the report. Alex — please add Dylan for infra questions on the calendar invite.

Best,
